observation.visible_scene: A close-up, centered view of a transparent stemmed wine glass against a flat, uniform pale-gray background. A thin, continuous stream of clear water falls from the top edge of the frame into the bowl, striking the liquid surface and forming a small dimple/splash crown at the point of impact. The glass holds a partial volume of aerated, bubble-filled clear water whose surface is uneven and sloshing.
visible_changes: The standing water level inside the glass rises gradually and steadily from the lower portion of the bowl (first frame) toward the mid-bowl (last frame).
The incoming stream remains present and roughly constant in position/angle throughout, with its bright highlight shifting slightly as it wobbles.
The water surface continuously deforms: waves and the splash crown at the impact point change shape and height frame to frame, sloshing from side to side.
The dense field of bubbles within the water churns and redistributes as the pour agitates the liquid.
The glass outline and the gray background stay fixed in size and position, indicating no evident camera pan/zoom; the only motion is the rising liquid and the surface turbulence.
outside_clip_unknowns: The container or source producing the stream is entirely out of frame.
The moment the pour began and the eventual final fill level (or whether the pour stops after the last frame) are not shown.
Any earlier surface state before t=0 is unknown; the turbulence is already ongoing at the first frame.
uncertain_details: Exact fill volume or precise rise rate is not measurable from the frames.
Whether minor apparent shifts of the glass are physical or camera-related is uncertain, though the static background argues against camera motion.
The identity of the liquid (water vs. another clear fluid) is inferred from appearance only.
